definition: A function $f$ with $f(x) \ge 0$ and total area $1$ under its graph that describes a continuous random variable: $\mathrm{P}(a \le X \le b) = \int_{a}^{b} f(x)\,\mathrm{d}x$.
A function defined by different formulas on different intervals of its domain, such as $f(x) = x^{2}$ for $0 \le x \le 1$ and $f(x) = 1$ for $1 < x \le 2$.

The expected squared distance of $X$ from its mean, $\mathrm{Var}(X) = \mathrm{E}\left[(X - \mu)^{2}\right] = \mathrm{E}(X^{2}) - \left[\mathrm{E}(X)\right]^{2}$; its square root is the standard deviation.
